column1: # The reference corpus: ten Java repositories the reading is read AGAINST, drawn at random from a stated
# frame. It is a denominator, not an answer key. No row here states a subject, and no row is scored.
# WHY IT EXISTS. The reading ranks a word by how far its density here departs from what a reference writes,
# and keeps the weakest claim any reference makes. One reference was an index: PlatformVocabulary reads the
# JDK's declared type names, where each name appears about once. Working Java writes the same words thousands
# of times, so a word common in working code departs enormously from a reference that names it once, and the
# ranking promoted exactly the words that should sink — `id` was the highest-ranked word in two of the nine
# evaluation-set members. Three filters were added to remove those words by rule. The doctrine refuses that:
# signals are votes, never gates. This file is the denominator those filters were standing in for.
# Columns: name, origin, sha, licence, rank, created, size
#   name      the directory the clone is expected under -Dcs.corpus.dir
#   origin    the URL it is cloned from
#   sha       the commit it is pinned to. A denominator read from a moving target moves under the reading.
#   licence   the SPDX identifier verified at that commit, or `none` where the repository states no licence.
#             A repository is read, never redistributed, so a repository stating no licence is recorded as
#             stating none rather than replaced — replacing it would be a choice, and the draw is not a choice.
#   rank      the position in the frame the seeded draw landed on, 0-based. It selects a time slice rather
#             than a repository — see THE DRAW. The seed reproduces the ranks and the ranks reproduce the rows.
#   created   the repository's creation time, which is the coordinate a rank is resolved through (see below)
#   size      the repository size in KB as GitHub states it, which is the variable the frame's floor bounds
# THE FRAME, fixed before the first row was drawn:
#   language:Java fork:false mirror:false size:>=1000 created:<2026-08-21
#   language:Java     the population this reading is about. GitHub states one primary language per repository.
#   fork:false        a fork is another repository's words copied. Counting them twice is a sampling defect,
#                     not a judgement about quality. GitHub's repository search excludes forks by default,
#                     so this qualifier changed the count by one and is stated to be explicit rather than
#                     to be relied on.
#   mirror:false      the same reason as forks.
#   size:>=1000       one megabyte. A STATED BOUND, NOT A DERIVED ONE, and it is the one number here that
#                     somebody could argue with. The reading estimates a density per word; a repository
#                     holding a handful of names gives a density dominated by which repository was drawn
#                     rather than by how Java is written. The measurement that settles it is leave-one-out
#                     over the ten — pool nine, read the tenth against them, and see how far the ranking
#                     moves. Until that is run, this floor is stated, not justified.
#   created:<...      a ceiling on creation time, so the frame is the same set on a later day. Without it the
#                     population grows between the first count and the last draw and the ranks mean nothing.
#   NOT in the frame, deliberately: stars, watchers, recent activity, whether the repository is archived, and
#   anything about what it contains. Each of those would select for maturity or for subject, and a reference
#   chosen for what it contains is the defect this file exists to remove.
# THE DRAW. Seed 20260821, Python's random.Random — Mersenne Twister — drawing uniform integers in [0, frame).
#   WHAT GITHUB'S COUNTS ARE WORTH, measured rather than assumed. total_count is exact and additive for a
#   result set up to about a million: a day, a month, a year and a four-year span each equalled the sum of
#   their two halves exactly, the largest at 1,081,460. Above that GitHub estimates, and the estimate is not
#   monotonic in a date bound — the same frame counted 3,833,338 repositories created before 2026-01-08 and
#   3,804,662 before 2026-01-22, a fortnight later. So EVERY QUERY THIS DRAW MAKES IS A BOUNDED RANGE HOLDING
#   FEWER THAN A MILLION REPOSITORIES, and no stage of it rests on an estimate.
#   1. Twenty yearly windows, counted exactly, give an exact cumulative index over the frame. Their sum is
#      4,154,178, which is the frame size stated below. A single query for the same frame returned 4,077,965,
#      3,980,293, 4,058,528 and 3,907,106 on four occasions within two hours; none of those is the number.
#   2. A rank picks its year from that index, then halves within it — every sub-window smaller than a year,
#      so every count still exact — until the window holds under a thousand, which is GitHub's page cap.
#   3. The rank's offset within that window indexes the page directly, ordered by creation time ascending.
#   TWO EARLIER IMPLEMENTATIONS WERE ABANDONED, BOTH BEFORE ANY ROW BELOW WAS DRAWN. The first resolved a
#   rank by cumulative arithmetic over unbounded `created:<t` queries, which are estimates: it produced
#   negative offsets, discarded them and redrew, biasing toward whatever GitHub happened to under-count. The
#   second kept the estimates but drew in two stages, a rank choosing a time slice and a second draw choosing
#   within it. That was worse for a reason the first hid: the estimate's error is around twenty thousand on
#   windows that truly hold a few dozen repositories, so the search halved on noise and would have converged
#   on an arbitrary instant. Neither ever accepted a row. An instrument replaced after seeing its output
#   would be a choice about that output; replaced before it has produced one, it is a repair.
#   REJECTIONS, stated before the draw and applied without exception: a rank landing on this repository or on
#   any of the nine evaluation-set members is rejected and replaced by the next draw from the same stream,
#   because a reference drawn from the corpus a reading is measured on is marking its own homework. A rank
#   landing on a repository already drawn is likewise replaced, as is one GitHub will not page. NOTHING ELSE
#   IS REJECTED — not subject, not size beyond the frame's floor, not activity, not licence, not appearance.
#   IN THE EVENT NOTHING WAS REJECTED: all ten ranks the seed produced were accepted, in order, first time.
#   THE DRAW WAS NOT RE-ROLLED. Where the composition below concentrates in one subject area, that is a fact
#   about this draw and is reported as one. Re-rolling until a sample looks representative is choosing.
#   THE DRAW AND ITS RECORD are docs/reference-corpus/draw.py and docs/reference-corpus/draw.json. The record
#   holds every range count the draw made, so the cumulative index can be checked without re-running it, and
#   the seed reproduces the ranks: random.Random(20260821) over 4,154,178 yields 4140166, 3827088, 324014,
# WHAT THIS COSTS TO CHANGE. Nothing here is edited. A different sample is a different file, named with
#   -Dcs.corpus.manifest, and the reason for two files is that ten is a small sample: whether a word sank
#   because every Java repository writes it, or because one drawn repository happened to be about it, is
#   answered by reading a second draw and comparing. Editing this one would destroy the comparison.
# ON THE DOCTRINE. A bundled vocabulary that votes must be a curated statement of a published standard, and
#   this is not a published standard. It is admissible because it is not curated: the frame is stated, the
#   draw is seeded, the rejections are exhaustive and recorded, and no repository here was picked for what it
#   contains. It is the same class of thing as the bundled English frequency list that already serves as the
#   other reference — a sampled denominator. If a future reader finds a repository in this list that was
#   chosen rather than drawn, the list is void.
# THE COMPOSITION OF THIS DRAW, stated before anything was read, from the repositories' own descriptions:
#   starwatchx                  a multi-camera space situational awareness prototype
#   liaobei                     an Xposed plugin for a Chinese messaging app
#   library-management-system   Java, Swing and MySQL
#   searchengine                "1st major Java Project"
#   ahsan                       "smd project"
#   hewanpedia                  "TugasUAS" — Indonesian for a final-examination assignment
#   mvc-template, overidle-launcher, memoire, websockettest   no description
#   ALL TEN CARRY ZERO STARS AND NO LICENCE. That is what uniform over 4,154,178 Java repositories looks
#   like: GitHub's Java is overwhelmingly coursework and hobby projects, and a draw returning ten maintained
#   libraries would have meant the frame was narrowed somewhere. It is reported, not corrected. No two of
#   the ten share a subject, which is the concentration risk the plan named, and it did not land.
#   WHAT IT MAY COST, stated before the reading rather than after it. These repositories write `id`, `get`,
#   `name` and `value`, so those will sink, which is what the reference is for. They may not write `log`,
#   `license`, `apache`, `builder` or `optional` — what MAINTAINED projects share, and all nine evaluation
#   members are maintained. If those survive as leading claims, the frame is wrong rather than the plan, and
#   the answer is a second sample from a second stated frame, compared against this one. The second frame is
#   stated in advance in docs/plans/A_CORPUS_NOT_AN_INDEX.md. It is never a filter on this draw's output.
#   THE LICENCE POSITION IS UNRESOLVED AND IS NOT THIS FILE'S TO SETTLE. Ten of ten state no licence, so
#   nothing grants a right to read them beyond GitHub's terms of service, which permit viewing and forking
#   public repositories. What would be bundled downstream is a table of word frequencies rather than any
#   code, and a frequency is a fact about a text rather than the text itself. That is a position, not a
#   ruling, and somebody has to take it before the pooled reference is published.
# Source: THIS PROJECT ran the draw; GitHub states the frame and the ranks. Drawn 2026-08-21, pinned and
#   licence-checked 2026-08-22. Each licence was read AT THE PINNED COMMIT through the repository licence
#   endpoint rather than at the branch head. The same check returns Apache-2.0 for apache/tika, so `none`
#   here is an absent licence file rather than a failed lookup.
